papers.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
papers.authors: Markus Fr\"ob, Albert Much
papers.abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.
papers.summary: The paper extends quantum metrology to relativistic QFT by defining the SLD quantum Fisher information on type III von Neumann algebras using Uhlmann's transition probability, and proves a sharp quantum Cramér–Rao bound for collective measurements. It shows that this bound equals the maximum classical Fisher information achievable by any measurement in the local region, thereby providing a rigorous precision limit for observers in QFT.

papers.title: General $\delta N$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
papers.authors: Amin Nassiri-Rad, Hassan Firouzjahi
papers.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $\delta N$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.
papers.summary: This paper develops a systematic graph‑theoretic classification of tree‑level higher‑order correlation functions in single‑field inflation via the δN formalism, deriving factorization of amplitudes into primary building blocks and extending the Suyama–Yamaguchi relation. It also presents all‑order expressions for vertex amplitudes in ultra‑slow‑roll scenarios, showing positivity and the possibility of cancellations for downward potential steps that can suppress leading local bispectrum and trispectrum while leaving higher‑point correlators non‑zero.

papers.title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
papers.authors: Akifumi Chitose, Hajime Fukuda, Kantaro Ohmori
papers.abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.
papers.summary: The paper studies the decay of a metastable vortex string in a supersymmetric U(2) gauge theory by mapping it to a D2-brane bounce in a Type IIA brane configuration. It shows that the D2-brane tension and bounce action match field-theory results, confirming the monopole pair creation picture.

papers.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski spacetimes
papers.authors: Finnian Gray, Hryhorii Ovcharenko
papers.abstract: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.
papers.summary: This paper extends recent breakthroughs in separating coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr–Newman spacetimes to the most general Plebański–Demiański family, using a chiral transformation and matrix R‑separation. It demonstrates that conformal symmetry yields a symmetry operator that decouples the chiral system, enabling a systematic treatment of perturbations in type‑D electro‑vacuum solutions.

papers.title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
papers.authors: Shohini Bhattacharya, Alexander Sang Yi
papers.abstract: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/\epsilon$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.
papers.summary: The authors identify that the anomalous poles appearing in one-loop box diagrams for gluon-initiated double deeply virtual Compton scattering arise from a subleading Landau singularity at the boundary of the Feynman‑parameter space, where a triangle subdiagram dominates. By analysing this endpoint with dimensional regularisation, non‑zero momentum transfer, and finite quark mass, they show how the same geometric origin produces the familiar 1/t anomaly pole, a new 1/m^2 behaviour, and the infrared evolution kernel common to all polarisation channels.
